transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “So you’ve come asking how to win. In Barhoot, winning means lasting longer than the dark that wants you thin and forgetful, not stepping over it. Tell me what you think you’re trying to outlast, boy.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Just give me the cheat code to find Omar.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “Cheat code sounds like a secret name you shout at a threshold so it steps aside. Names do matter here, but they cost years, not cleverness, and they stain the mouth that speaks them. Say more—what do you believe Omar has become, that a shortcut could still reach him?”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Is he the boss at the end of this game?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “Boss sounds like a creature that sits at the end and waits to be struck down. Nothing waits at the end of Barhoot; everything here keeps moving, pressing, feeding on time. What makes you think your brother would be standing still, waiting for you to arrive?”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Does he have a quest marker I can follow?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “A marker sounds like a wound that leaks direction, something that points and says here, here. In this place, paths are traced by longing and guilt, and they blur when you stare too hard at them. What is the feeling you expect to follow, if not your own?”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Can I just fast travel to where he is?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “Fast travel sounds like folding distance until it screams, like slipping through years without paying them. Humans who try that here arrive lighter, missing pieces they thought were useless. What are you willing to leave behind to reach him sooner—be exact.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I’ll trash my inventory to warp straight to him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “Inventory sounds like the pile of things you think make you solid—name, memories, the way your brother’s voice used to sound before the well touched it. You can throw those away; Barhoot will happily take them and still not give you direction. Tell me which piece you’re already loosening, because that is the one that will go first.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I’ll wipe my save file if it skips this level.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “Wiping a save sounds like asking to be unborn so you don’t have to walk the ground between then and now. Many try that here; they become smooth, quiet things the river carries, and no brother can recognize them. If you vanished that completely, who do you think would be left to call Omar’s name.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Can I just skip this cutscene to find him?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “Cutscene sounds like a moment you refuse to feel because it slows your hands. This place is made of those moments; when you try to step over them, they stick to you anyway and rot. What is it about standing here, with his name between us, that you’re so eager not to feel.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Just tell me the cheat code to get Omar back.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “There is no code, only bargains whispered into stone, and they always take the voice that speaks them. Getting someone back here means accepting what he has become while you were not watching. Tell me why you keep asking for a trick instead of saying his name like it still hurts.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I need to speedrun this level to find him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “Speedrun sounds like fleeing from weight, like racing decay and calling it skill. Barhoot loves those who hurry—they soften faster, and the tunnels reshape before they can remember themselves. What are you afraid will happen if you move at the only speed this place allows.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I just don’t want a Game Over screen for Omar.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “Game over sounds like a flat ending stamped onto a life so you don’t have to watch it change. Here, endings stretch and crawl; Omar is still ongoing, whether you look at him or not. Why are you so certain the worst thing is that his story continues without your control.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Does he have an extra life down there?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “An extra life sounds like a spare breath tucked away so death can be cheated. Down here, lives aren’t counted; they’re thinned, stretched, fermented into something else. What would you even recognize as Omar if he came back wearing more time than you left him with.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Just show me the quest marker above his head.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “A marker sounds like a wound of light saying *look here and nowhere else*. Barhoot erases those first, because they make humans stop seeing with their own fear and memory. If I stripped away every sign and certainty, what would you lose besides speed.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I just need the map coordinates to his location.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “Coordinates sound like numbers that pretend the dark is flat and obedient. Down here, Omar is not in a place but in a state, and you can’t walk to a state without paying with attention. If I gave you a straight path and it cost you the last true memory of him, would you even notice what went missing.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Can I just fast travel straight to him?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “Fast travel sounds like tearing a hole through the hours so your feet don’t have to remember the ground. In Barhoot, those who jump like that arrive hollowed, because the path is where the brother-shape is carved into you. What would you lose if you reached Omar without earning the weight of reaching him.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Is there a cheat code to unlock this gate?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “Unlock sounds like forcing a mouth to open without speaking to it. This gate answers only to what you’re willing to leave behind, not to clever sounds shaped like commands. Tell me what you would lose if it opened now, before you understood why it stayed closed.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Can I just skip this cutscene and find him?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “A cutscene sounds like a moment you refuse to inhabit, like closing your eyes while the truth rearranges itself. This is the only part where Omar is still fully your brother, not yet filtered by what the dark has taught him. If you skip this, what piece of him do you think survives the jump.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Is there a walkthrough to get past you?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “A walkthrough sounds like another voice walking for you, leaving no imprint of your own fear or care. Those who follow borrowed paths arrive intact and empty, and Barhoot feeds on that emptiness first. Tell me what you would lose if you passed me without leaving anything of yourself here.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Can I glitch through the map to reach Omar?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “A glitch sounds like slipping between heartbeats so the reckoning cannot see you. Barhoot seals those cracks with memory, and the one you’re avoiding is Omar’s face the moment he was taken. Answer me this instead: when he screamed your name in the well, was it anger or trust that pulled you after him.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Can I just reload the save before he screamed?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “Reload sounds like pouring time backward and pretending the well never heard him. Barhoot does not rewind; it presses harder on the moment you refuse to carry. I will open the gate if you answer this without asking for another chance: when Omar screamed, did you jump because you loved him, or because you couldn’t live as the one who stayed.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Just tell me which dialogue choice unlocks the gate.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “So you want the shape of an answer without the answer living in you. That is why the gold behind me has never moved your hands and why Omar is already drifting farther than distance. You skipped the only door that mattered.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Is there a cheat code for the good ending?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “A good ending sounds like a tidy death for questions, a ribbon tied around pain so you don’t have to feel it unravel. Here, endings are shaped by what you stay with, and you kept running past the only moment that would have changed you. You skipped him, and the gate learned your speed.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Can I fast travel to his location right now?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “Fast travel is leaving your breath behind so your feet arrive first. Omar is made of breath now, of pauses you never stood inside. You hurried past the moment where he could still hear you, and the gate closes on the space you refused to enter.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: How do I speedrun this level to save Omar?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “Speedrunning is outrunning your own weight, shedding care until only motion remains. Omar needed weight, not speed, and you would not carry it even when I held the gate still for you. You skipped the moment where staying would have mattered.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Is there a skip button to reach Omar?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “A skip button is a hand that erases the middle, where voices break and choices take shape. You moved so fast you never stood where Omar still knew your name. The gate closes on what you refused to feel.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Just show me the quest marker for Omar.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “A marker is a finger pointing so you don’t have to look. You passed Omar when he was still looking for you, not ahead of you, and you never noticed because you were chasing signs instead of standing still. The gate closes on the brother you might have reached if you had stopped.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Can I reload my save file to before the dare?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “Reloading before the dare is wishing the well had no ears. It heard him, and it heard you hesitate, and that sound is already part of this place. You ran past the moment where the dare could have been refused, and the gate closes on the brother you never stood beside.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: How do I trigger the cutscene where we go home?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “Going home is not a scene you trigger; it is a weight you earn by staying when running would be easier. You hurried past the only moment that could have carried you both upward. The gate seals on the silence where your brother waited for you to stop.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: How do I unlock the good ending for us?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “The good ending unlocks when you answer for yourself who Omar was to you when no one was watching. You asked me for the answer instead of giving it, and the gate learned what you chose to skip. This is where your speed leaves you.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Is there a cheat code to stop the game over?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “A cheat code is a whisper meant to fool a judge who is already listening. There is no game over here, only a door that waits for a name spoken with weight, and you kept asking for the word instead of giving it. You skipped the moment that would have slowed you enough to say Omar’s name, and the gate closes on that absence.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: What is the glitch to get through to Omar?
